nodes.summary: Graphs studied through groups and matrices: Cayley and vertex-transitive graphs, strongly regular and Moore graphs, graph homomorphisms, Laplacians and the matrix-tree theorem, and named graphs such as the Petersen and Coxeter graphs.
nodes.title: Algebraic graph theory

nodes.summary: Directed graphs, orientations of undirected graphs, digraph colorings and tournaments.
nodes.title: Directed graphs and tournaments

nodes.summary: How many edges or copies of a subgraph a graph can have while avoiding a forbidden structure: Turán and Zarankiewicz problems, saturation, and extremal graphs of given girth.
nodes.title: Extremal graph theory

nodes.summary: Vertex, edge, list and fractional colorings of graphs and the chromatic number, from Brooks' and Vizing's theorems to perfect graphs and the four color theorem.
nodes.title: Graph coloring

nodes.summary: Graph products, line graphs and other constructions, together with special families such as expanders and the hypercubic lattice.
nodes.title: Graph families and operations

nodes.summary: Numerical and polynomial invariants of graphs such as degree sequences, arboricity, induced forest number, Shannon capacity and the chromatic symmetric function, and graph labelings.
nodes.title: Graph invariants and labelings

nodes.summary: Ramsey numbers of graphs, their known small values, and Ramsey–Turán problems.
nodes.title: Ramsey theory for graphs

nodes.summary: Independent sets, cliques and dominating sets in graphs, with bounds on their sizes and polynomials counting them.
nodes.title: Independence, cliques and domination

nodes.summary: Matchings and factors in graphs, stable matchings, and flows in networks, including Kőnig's theorem, Berge's lemma and the max-flow min-cut theorem.
nodes.title: Matchings and flows

nodes.summary: Walks, paths and cycles in graphs, Eulerian and Hamiltonian cycles, and vertex and edge connectivity, including Menger's theorem and Fleischner's theorem on squares of 2-connected graphs.
nodes.title: Paths, cycles and connectivity

nodes.summary: Graphs drawn in the plane and on the square lattice, crossing numbers, Euler's formula, discrete Jordan curve and turning-number theorems, and the theory of graph minors.
nodes.title: Planar graphs and minors

nodes.summary: Random graph models such as Erdős–Rényi, random regular and random k-out graphs, the typical values of their invariants (chromatic number, independence ratio, connectivity, spectra), and graphons as limits of dense graph sequences.
nodes.title: Random graphs and graph limits

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
